The story makes sophisticated use of idiom, as well as regional dialect, to lend authenticity to the characters' voices and ground the setting in the Oderbruch region. For example, Hradscheck uses colloquial German idioms such as "seine fünf Sinne beisammen haben" (to have one's wits about one/have one's five senses together) and "Du weißt ja Bescheid" (you know the drill/score) to sound like a natural, pragmatic shopkeeper. Furthermore, the author uses the Low German (Plattdeutsch) regional dialect for the neighbor, Mother Jeschke ("Joa, et wahrd nu Tied. De Malvesieren kümmen all von sülwst"), which contrasts with Hradscheck's more standard spoken German and highlights their distinct social standings and backgrounds.
